question.problem:
Determine if the matrix 
$A=[\begin{aligned}7 & -12 \\ 4 & -7\end{aligned}]$ 
is diagonalizable or not, and if it is diagonalizable, find a corresponding diagonal matrix $D.$
question.worked_solution:
First, we find the eigenvalues of the matrix $A$ by solving $det(A-\lambda I)=0$:

$$
\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}7-\lambda  & -12 \\ 4 & -7-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (7-\lambda )(-7-\lambda )-4\cdot (-12) & =0 \\ {\lambda }^{2}-1 & =0 \\ (\lambda +1)(\lambda -1) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

So, the eigenvalues are ${\lambda }_{1}=1$ and ${\lambda }_{2}=-1.$ Since we get two distinct eigenvalues, the matrix $A$ is diagonalizable.

Now, we construct the diagonal matrix $D,$ as follows:

$$
D=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}]
$$
